intro: A harness is the durable layer around a model: procedures, constraints, memory, patterns, and human gates. The model is powerful; the harness is what makes Monday morning repeatable.

layers.title: Cockpit
layers.subtitle: Codex primary · Cursor compatible
layers.body: Codex is now the daily task, worktree and review surface. Cursor remains supported. Neither owns the working relationship: portable skills and proof classes outlive the host; guidance and permissions stay native to it.
tips: Codex project guidance in AGENTS.md
Portable procedures in Agent Skills
Worktrees isolate state; one writer still owns each tree

layers.title: Skills
layers.subtitle: How to do a job
layers.body: Thin, named procedures the agent loads when a task matches. Detail lives on demand so every turn stays cheap. A skill earns its place by preventing a repeated failure.
tips: Trigger nouns in the description so the host can select it
Separate SKILL.md (short) from reference.md (deep)
Include an explicit proof of done

layers.title: Rules
layers.subtitle: What must never go wrong
layers.body: Fail-closed constraints: secrets stay out of chat, outbound needs approval, scripts must not clobber source. Few always-on; most requestable.
tips: Always-on budget is sacred
One symptom → one rule when possible
Write the incident in one line under Why

layers.title: Secrets vault (Bitwarden)
layers.subtitle: Two planes — humans vs agents
layers.body: Captured passwords and API tokens must never enter the AI conversation. We use Bitwarden Password Manager for human logins and Bitwarden Secrets Manager for machine secrets agents resolve — filled through desktop dialogs, not chat paste.
tips: Desktop capture → vault; agent confirms length only
Password Manager ≠ Secrets Manager — keep the planes separate
Never put vault tokens or secret values in skills, git, or chat

layers.title: Memory (MemPalace)
layers.subtitle: Curated palace, not a transcript dump
layers.body: We use MemPalace as the durable-memory layer: searchable drawers and a light knowledge graph for decisions, stances, tickets, and signed patterns.
tips: Write with a retention reason
File by wing/room so agents can find the shelf
Invalidate stale facts instead of stacking contradictions
Enrich provenance instead of invalidate-first rewrites
Prove later retrieval helped before calling a memory durable

layers.title: Patterns
layers.subtitle: Kaizen → Hansei → Toyota Way Practices
layers.body: Cross-cutting ways of working: propose → human sign-off → encode → apply → periodic Hansei. The learning core is named Toyota Way Practices; patterns are the registry that makes Kaizen real.
tips: No silent promotion to signed-off
Hansei keeps / amends / retires — on a cadence
Toyota Way Practices names the cluster; load the member practice for the live pain
Encode into skills/rules where agents will load them

layers.title: Human gates
layers.subtitle: Irreversible stays human
layers.body: Desktop decisions for forks that matter. The referent (draft, command, path) must be visible in the ask — not implied by chat order. Runtime policy (Preloop) layers under these gates — it does not replace them.
tips: One gate for irreversible outbound — not soft nag stacks
Name who acts: human vs agent
Danger chrome for destructive arms
Layer Preloop audit under P0; never swap consent for a firewall alone

layers.title: Runtime + routing
layers.subtitle: Preloop · OpenRouter
layers.body: Preloop adds a durable policy/audit plane on tool use — and a Cloud PR reviewer that posts a `preloop` commit status. OpenRouter routes models for the cockpit and that reviewer. Both serve the harness; neither is the harness.
tips: Keep keys in a vault
Document methods, not enrollment secrets
Route models deliberately; still require proof class

layers.title: Parallel lanes
layers.subtitle: Team-shaped solo work
layers.body: Named agent lanes with clear ownership and handoffs. Useful for product loops; dangerous without co-prosperity on shared benches and trees.
tips: Declare owns / never at session start
Handoffs are explicit tickets
Do not run two writers on one tree
Budget review load and scarce host/bench resources

layers.title: Channels & media
layers.subtitle: WhatsApp · ingest · voice
layers.body: Messaging (Briar on WhatsApp), voice notes, and purposeful file/image ingest are harness surfaces — same fail-closed outbound rules as the cockpit.
tips: One watcher per live channel
Ingest for the task; curate into memory
Voice is a medium, not a privilege escalation

layers.title: Token lean
layers.subtitle: Context is rent
layers.body: Measure always-on tax and tool-result payloads. Keep skills thin, rules requestable, specialty tools task-scoped, and parallel lanes bounded instead of growing one mega-context.
tips: SKILL.md short; reference.md deep
Pulse when sessions feel heavy
Catalog bloat is a bug
Bound tool output before it enters the conversation

layers.title: Harness self-evals
layers.subtitle: Test the guardrails, not only the code
layers.body: A versioned adversarial corpus exercises secrets, consequential writes, prompt injection and tool-loop behavior. Sensors and circuit breakers catch drift before confidence becomes policy.
tips: Keep a known-answer corpus and thresholds
Add real failures after privacy review
Stop repeated tool/error loops explicitly
